# Marseille ACC (East)
## Area of Responsibility and Sectorisation
The lateral and vertical limits of the area of responsibility, together with the applicable sectorisation, are described on the dedicated **Sectorisation** page for [**Marseille ACC (East)**](https://doc.vatsim.fr/en/atc/SOPs/LFMM/sectorisation).

# Transfer of Control & Communication
## Transfer of Control
Unless otherwise specified in this Local Operating Procedure, Transfer of Control shall take place at the common Area of Responsibility (AoR) boundary.

If the receiving ATS unit is marked as **BREAK** in EuroScope, the standard hand-off procedures defined in this Letter of Agreement are suspended. In this case, transfer of communications shall only take place after the receiving ATS unit has assumed control of the aircraft using the appropriate EuroScope coordination function.

If an ATS unit needs to reduce or suspend transfers, the adjacent ATS unit(s) shall be notified whenever practicable. A minimum notification period of 5 minutes should be provided where operationally feasible.

While transfers are suspended, the standard hand-off procedures defined in this Letter of Agreement shall not apply until normal operations have resumed.

## Silent Transfer of Control
Unless otherwise specified in this document, a minimum spacing of **5 NM** may be used for the silent transfer of control between adjacent sectors within Langen FIR for aircraft at the same level and following identical or converging routes.

The transferring controller shall ensure that the applicable spacing is maintained for at least **20 NM** within the receiving sector and that separation is not infringed.

Whenever practicable, the same spacing should also be applied to aircraft inbound to the same destination at different levels in order to maintain a consistent traffic flow.

Subject to prior coordination, the required spacing may be achieved on average. In all cases, responsibility for maintaining separation remains with the transferring controller.

## Transfer of Communication
Transfer of communications shall take place no later than Transfer of Control.

## Hand-Off procedure
Unless otherwise agreed between stations online, the following hand-off procedure shall apply:
1.	The upstream sector sends the aircraft to the frequency of the downstream sector by voice or text.
2.	The upstream sector initiates a transfer via the appropriate function of the radar client.
3.	Upon initial call the downstream sector assumes the flight via the appropriate function of the radar client.

## SSR Code Assignment
Both ATS units shall transfer flights on verified discrete SSR codes. Any change of SSR code by the accepting ATS unit may only take place after the Transfer of Control point.

Where the aircraft is equipped and capable, Mode S identification using SSR Code 1000 should be used as the preferred method of identification transfer. Where the use of a discrete SSR code is required, SSR codes shall be assigned in accordance with the applicable ORCAM allocation or other VATSIM network-approved SSR code allocation scheme.

# Procedures for Coordination
## Definitions
A release authorizes the accepting ATS unit to climb, descend, and/or turn a specific aircraft by up to 45° before the transfer of control. Unless otherwise coordinated, the transferring ATS unit remains responsible for maintaining separation within its Area of Responsibility.

Unless otherwise specified, any reference to a VATSIM ATS callsign in this Local Operating Procedure also applies to any higher ATS unit assuming that position's responsibilities (e.g. APP procedures also apply when the corresponding CTR provides approach services).

References to ATS callsigns include all valid sectorized variations (e.g. procedures applicable to LFMM_RAE_CTR also apply to LFMM_U_CTR, LFMM_CTR, and other sectorized variants).

## General Conditions
Unless otherwise specified in this Local Operating Procedure, all aircraft shall be coordinated via the published Coordination Points (COPs) and transferred using a valid COP. Any deviation from the published procedures shall be coordinated between the concerned ATS units by voice, text, or EuroScope inter-sector coordination.

Aircraft shall be transferred at the flight levels specified in this Letter of Agreement. If this is not possible due to the aircraft's Requested Flight Level (RFL), it shall be transferred at its RFL, provided no traffic conflict exists; otherwise, coordination is required.

Any traffic situation not covered by this Letter of Agreement shall be individually coordinated between the concerned ATS units.
Unless explicitly released or otherwise specified, transfer of communications does not constitute transfer of control. The transferring ATS unit shall retain control until the transfer of control point is reached.

The following notation is used throughout this Local Operating Procedure:

- **↑FLxxx / ↓FLxxx** – Climb or descend to the specified flight level, unless additional restrictions are stated.
- **FLxxxA** – Climbing through and above the specified flight level.
- **FLxxxB** – Descending through and below the specified flight level.
- Any crossing altitude, speed restriction, or other condition shall be stated separately 	where applicable.
